html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. API: application programming interface

  • Context engineering: deciding what goes into the context window, in what order, and for how long
  • Preventing context drift and bloat: tool output pruning and compaction
  • Context isolation with subagents or multi-step workflows
  • Memory outside the window

2The Context Is a Budget

Running case

Tidewater's Assistant Gets Confused Late in the Day

  • Adjusters keep one long session open all day
  • Each question pulls in large policy lookups and 40-field claim records
  • By afternoon the assistant repeats itself, ignores early instructions and costs more per question

  • Everything in the window competes for attention: system prompt, instructions, tool definitions, history, documents and tool results. More is not better; relevant and well ordered is better.
  • Context drift: the model gradually loses track of early instructions or facts as the window fills with later material.
  • Context bloat: tokens spent on irrelevant content (verbose tool output, stale history) raise cost and latency and lower quality.
Exam tip

Context problems (drift, repetition, rising cost) are fixed by managing the context, not by buying a bigger window.

3Techniques

Technique What it does Use when
Tool output pruning Trim tool results to the fields that matter before they enter the context; or clear old tool results (context editing) A tool returns far more than the next step needs
Compaction (summarization) Replace older turns with a summary (server-side compaction, or your own summarizing call) A long conversation nears the limit
Context isolation Do verbose work in a subagent or a separate step and bring back a short result Exploration, search or analysis would flood the main context
Multi-step workflows Break work into steps, each with only the context it needs A single huge prompt is slow, costly and hard to debug
External memory Save key facts to files or a store and load them when relevant (a memory tool) Facts must survive beyond the window or across sessions
Retrieval just in time Fetch documents when needed instead of loading everything up front Large corpora
Ordering Put long documents first and the question and instructions last; keep stable content before volatile content (caching) Long-context prompts

  • Compaction risks: a summary can lose exact numbers, dates and commitments. Keep such facts in a separate persistent block that is re-sent each turn, and test what the summary preserves.
  • Do not drop what the next step needs; prune by relevance, not just by age.
  • Session hygiene helps: a fresh session per task is the cheapest context management (Module 4).

[Verify live] The API offers server-side compaction (beta) for long conversations and context editing to clear old tool results; models differ in whether they track their remaining context. As of 8 November 2026.

Exam tip

Symptoms of drift and bloat (ignores early rules, repeats itself, slow and costly) point to pruning, compaction, isolation or a fresh session, not to a bigger model.

Exam tip

Exact figures and commitments must not pass through a summary: keep them in a separate persistent block.

4Exam Q&A

S1Late in a long session the assistant ignores early instructions and each answer is slower and costlier. What is the most direct improvement?

  • ATurn off the system prompt so that it cannot be ignored any more
  • BIncrease max_tokens
  • CSwitch to a larger model
  • DPrune tool output, compact older turns, or start a fresh session
Show the answer

Answer: D. Drift and bloat come from a crowded context; reduce and reorganize what the model has to carry.

S2A tool returns 40 fields per claim, but only five matter for the next step. What should the developer do?

  • AAsk the model to ignore the rest
  • BDisable the tool
  • CTrim the result to the relevant fields before it enters the context
  • DPass the full record each time, including fields the model never needs
Show the answer

Answer: C. Tool output pruning keeps the window lean without losing what the next step needs.

S3A long conversation will soon exceed the context window. Which technique replaces older turns with a shorter version?

  • ACompaction by summarizing earlier turns
  • BRaising the temperature so the model needs less context
  • CBatch processing
  • DStreaming
Show the answer

Answer: A. Compaction summarizes older history into a shorter form, which frees room in the window for new turns.

S4After compaction the assistant forgets an exact deductible amount a customer stated earlier. What is the best remedy?

  • ADelete the conversation
  • BSummarize more aggressively
  • CAsk the customer to repeat all of the earlier details again at the start of every single turn
  • DKeep exact figures in a facts block that is re-sent every turn, outside the summary
Show the answer

Answer: D. Critical exact facts should not pass through summarization.

S5An exploration task reads dozens of files and would flood the main conversation. What is a good design?

  • AUse a larger window and hope
  • BHave a subagent explore in its own context and return a short summary
  • CSkip the exploration
  • DPaste every file into the main context so the model has everything at once
Show the answer

Answer: B. Isolation keeps verbose work out of the main context.

S6For a prompt with a long contract and a question about it, how should the content be ordered?

  • AThe long document first, then the question and instructions
  • BOrder does not matter at all, so any layout works equally well
  • CThe question first, then the contract placed after it near the end
  • DThe question in the middle of the document
Show the answer

Answer: A. Putting long material first and the query last generally improves results.

S7Which TWO belong to good context engineering? Select TWO.

  • AKeep every tool result forever
  • BLoad documents only when needed instead of all up front
  • CPut volatile text before stable text in a cached prompt
  • DSave durable facts outside the window and load them when relevant
  • ENever summarize anything
Show the answer

Answer: B, D. Retrieve just in time and use external memory; keep stable text first for caching.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Context A budget: everything competes for attention, cost and latency
Drift / bloat Early rules ignored, repetition / irrelevant tokens, higher cost
Pruning Trim or clear tool results; keep only fields the next step needs
Compaction Summarize older turns; keep exact facts in a separate block
Isolation Subagents or separate steps return short results
Memory External files or store; load when relevant
Ordering Long documents first, question last; stable before volatile
Hygiene Fresh session per task
